newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan crude imports down 16.1 percent in July.
newsitem.headline: Japan crude imports down 16.1 percent in July.

text.p: Japan imported 18 million kilolitres (kl) of crude oil in July, down 16.1 percent from the same month a year earlier, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Monday.

A MITI official told reporters that there was no specific reason for the decline. He attributed the decrease to the shipment schedule of importers. "It's mostly a matter of scheduling for crude oil shipments," the MITI official said.
Crude oil imports fell from most areas, with the exception of shipments from Latin America which rose 91.6 percent from July 1995.
Crude oil from Latin America, however, only accounted for 3.1 percent of all crude oil imports.
Japan imports the majority of its crude oil from the Middle East. Imports from that area accounted for 78.3 percent of Japan's imports for July.

The United Arab Emirates -- which produces crude grades such as Dubai and Murban -- was the largest source of crude oil for Japan. It accounted for 5.5 million kl, or 30.3 percent of all imports in July. It was followed by Saudi Arabia and Indonesia, where Japan imported 3.4 million kl and 1.5 million kl, respectively, in July.
No crude oil imports were reported from West Africa in June or July.

Japanese importers often buy crude oil from that area when the differential between Brent and Dubai quotes is wide, making West African crudes economically attractive. The quotes for West African crudes are usually linked to Brent. Crude throughput amounted to 19.8 million kl in July, up 3.4 percent from the same period a year earlier. It represented a year-on-year increase for the third consecutive month.
Some 1.5 million kl of crude oil was diverted for use by electric utilities in July, up 31.7 percent from July 1995.
